properties.natural_language: An attestation received via gossip (EDGE-RECEIVE-GOSSIP) must have a valid committee_bits field that references an existing committee for the current epoch.
An attestation received from gossip must contain a valid BLS signature over the AttestationData before committee membership verification.
The DATA-ATTESTATION and DATA-COMMITTEE-BITS fields in gossip-received attestations must be well-formed SSZ-encoded data within maximum size limits.
After committee membership verification succeeds, the attester's validator index must be confirmed present in the committee indicated by committee_bits.
After gossip mutation detection (membership invalid), the attestation must be discarded and never stored in any local cache or forwarded to peers.
After aggregation of identical votes, the resulting aggregate must contain exactly the union of all individual attestation signatures for the same (beacon_block_root, source, target) tuple.
After aggregate signature verification, the aggregated BLS signature must be valid against all participating validators' public keys.
The index field within the signed AttestationData must always be zero in EIP-7549; the committee index is only carried in the outer container's committee_bits field.
The number of attestations in a block must not exceed MAX_ATTESTATIONS, and the number of attester slashings must not exceed 1 per block.
Block size must remain within acceptable bounds (~488KB worst case per slashing on 1M validators) after all attestations and slashings are included.
A pre-Electra attestation crossing the fork boundary must be rejected; only Electra-format attestations (with committee_bits) are valid post-fork.
At most one epoch of offline penalty may be incurred by a validator whose attestation is rejected at the fork boundary.
The 62x improvement in pairing operations applies when attestations from multiple committees share the same (beacon_block_root, source, target) and can be aggregated cross-committee.
The wallet_addEthereumChain request from a dapp (EDGE-DAPP-REQUEST) must contain a valid chainId field in hexadecimal (0x-prefixed) format per EIP-155.
The rpcUrls array in the chain addition request must be non-empty and all URLs must use the HTTPS scheme; HTTP and file: schemes must be rejected.
The chain ID returned by eth_chainId on the provided RPC endpoints must match the submitted chainId value; mismatches indicate a potentially malicious configuration.
After user approval and chain storage, the new chain must be persisted in the wallet's chain registry with the submitted chainId (not the RPC-reported ID) to prevent signing attacks.
After any validation failure, the wallet must return an appropriate error to the dapp without revealing which specific check failed to prevent information leakage about wallet state.
A chain must never be added to the wallet without explicit user consent; automated chain additions are prohibited.
The user must be informed of the requesting dapp's identity and warned about RPC endpoint privacy exposure before making consent decisions.
The wallet must use only the submitted chainId for transaction signing purposes, never substituting or trusting a chain ID reported by the RPC endpoint.
If a nativeCurrency object is provided, it must contain valid name, symbol, and non-negative decimals fields.
Wallet confirmations should be shown even for duplicate chain requests to prevent information leakage about which chains are already configured.
An incoming UDP packet (EDGE-RECEIVE-PACKET) must not exceed 1280 bytes and must contain a valid 16-byte masking IV followed by an AES-CTR masked header.
After unmasking, the protocol-id field must equal 'discv5' and the version field must be a supported version; otherwise the packet must be dropped.
NODES response records (EDGE-RECEIVE-NODES) must contain valid, self-signed ENR records; records with invalid signatures must be discarded.
After successful handshake verification, both nodes must share identical session encryption keys derived from the same ECDH shared secret.
After AES-GCM decryption succeeds with a valid GCM tag, the message content is guaranteed authentic and unmodified.
After routing table update, a k-bucket must contain at most 16 entries; if full, the least-recently-seen node must be pinged for liveness before eviction.
Every nonce used for AES-GCM encryption must be unique per session; the first 32 bits encode the outgoing message counter to prevent nonce reuse.
Header masking using the destination node ID as AES-CTR key must prevent passive observers from identifying packet recipients without knowing the node ID.
The id-signature in a handshake message must prove the sender's identity by signing the id-nonce from the WHOAREYOU challenge with the sender's static key.
A lookup terminates only after the k closest known nodes to the target have been queried and responded or timed out.
No packet-level retransmission occurs; reliability is achieved at the lookup algorithm level by querying multiple nodes.
The EIP-7441 fork epoch must be a multiple of RUN_DURATION_IN_EPOCHS for Whisk shuffling alignment to be correct.
Fork activation requires state.slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH == 0 AND the epoch equals EIP7441_FORK_EPOCH; activation at non-epoch-boundary slots is invalid.
After upgrade_to_eip7441 completes, every validator must have a whisk_tracker, k_commitment, and the proposer/candidate tracker arrays must be populated.
After the three post-upgrade selection operations complete atomically, whisk_proposer_trackers must be fully populated for the next day of proposals.
A validator's Whisk secret k must not be derivable from the publicly stored k-commitment or tracker at any point during or after initialization.
The retroactive candidate selection must use epoch offset saturating_sub(epoch, PROPOSER_SELECTION_GAP + 1) to prevent seed collision with proposer selection randomness.
All existing Capella state fields must be preserved exactly during the upgrade; the transformation only adds new Whisk fields.
A gossip message from a peer (EDGE-PEER-SENDS-GOSSIP) must be snappy-compressed and the uncompressed payload must not exceed 10 MiB (MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE).
An oversized message from a peer (EDGE-OVERSIZED-DROP) must be immediately dropped and the peer penalized via scoring.
Message timestamps must be within MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY (500ms) of the local clock (EDGE-CLOCK-CHECK); messages outside this window must be rejected or ignored.
A new peer connection (EDGE-NEW-PEER) must immediately trigger a mandatory Status message exchange before any other protocol interaction.
The SSZ-snappy length prefix in received messages must be minimally encoded and not exceed 10 bytes.
After beacon block gossip validation passes, the block must have a valid proposer signature, a known parent, and a slot not in the future.
After attestation gossip validation passes, the attestation must have a valid committee index, matching epoch, single participating validator, and valid BLS signature.
After message rejection, the sending peer's reputation score must be decremented; persistent low scores must trigger disconnection.
After fork digest check, peers with mismatched fork digests must be immediately disconnected.
The message ID computation must use MESSAGE_DOMAIN_VALID_SNAPPY for valid payloads and MESSAGE_DOMAIN_INVALID_SNAPPY for invalid payloads to enable correct deduplication.
Block range requests must be bounded to a maximum of 1024 blocks per request to prevent resource exhaustion.
A node must maintain subscriptions to exactly 2 persistent attestation subnets, deterministically computed from the node ID, rotated every EPOCHS_PER_SUBNET_SUBSCRIPTION (256 epochs).
The target GossipSub mesh size must be maintained at D=8 peers (range 6-12) to ensure message propagation resilience against Sybil attacks.
Block number data used for difficulty calculation (EDGE-READ-BLOCK-NUM) must be the authentic current block height from a validated parent chain.
A block header received from a network peer (EDGE-RECEIVE-HEADER) must include a valid difficulty field that can be verified against the expected computation.
After applying the bomb delay, the fake block number must equal max(0, actual_block_number - 9,000,000).
After difficulty comparison, a block with difficulty not equal to the computed expected difficulty must be rejected.
After block state transition completes, the post-state root must equal the deterministic Merkle Patricia trie root of the final world state.
The bomb component is always computed as 2^((fake_block_number // 100000) - 2), ensuring exponential growth of difficulty over time.
Block rewards must be credited only to the miner account and uncle block producers; no other accounts may receive rewards during block processing.
Parent block timestamps used for difficulty calculation must be within 900 seconds of actual time to prevent difficulty manipulation.
A block received from a peer (EDGE-PEER-SENDS-BLOCK) must include a valid block number to determine the applicable consensus ruleset.
Block header and body data received from peers must be well-formed and deserializable before fork-based ruleset determination.
After checking the block number against the activation threshold, the correct ruleset (pre-Byzantium or Byzantium) must be applied; blocks at or above 4,370,000 use Byzantium rules.
All 9 Byzantium component EIPs (100, 140, 196, 197, 198, 211, 214, 649, 658) must activate atomically at the fork block; no partial activation is permitted.
The fork block number must be correctly configured per network: 4,370,000 for mainnet, 1,700,000 for Ropsten, or a custom value from genesis configuration.
Blocks that do not follow the appropriate ruleset for their block number must be rejected; non-upgraded peers will fork off onto an incompatible chain.
After EIP editor merges a properly formatted submission, the EIP must transition to Draft status and receive an incremental EIP number.
After Last Call deadline passes without normative changes, the EIP must transition to Final status; if normative changes are needed, it must return to Review.
A withdrawn EIP cannot be resurrected; withdrawal is a permanent terminal state.
An EIP in Final status must not receive normative changes; only errata and non-normative clarifications are permitted.
An EIP must be automatically marked Stagnant after 6 months of inactivity in Draft, Review, or Last Call status.

An EIP submission must include a valid RFC 822 preamble, title (max 44 chars), description (max 140 chars), required sections (Abstract, Specification, Rationale, Security Considerations), and CC0 copyright waiver.
An EIP without an adequate Security Considerations section must be blocked from progressing to Final status.
External links in EIPs must anchor to specific commits or versions; mutable links that could change after finalization are prohibited.
Core EIPs require AllCoreDevs discussion and cross-client implementation consensus before finalization; unilateral advancement is prohibited.
A stagnant EIP can be resurrected back to Draft status by the author or an editor, but only via a new PR submission.
An account entry in the state trie must have at least one non-trivial property (non-empty code, non-zero nonce, or non-zero balance) to be valid post-merge.
No empty accounts (zero code, zero nonce, zero balance) may exist in the post-merge state trie; their presence indicates undefined behavior.
On Ethereum mainnet (identified by merge block hash 0x56a9bb...76a664), all empty accounts were cleared before the merge transition, guaranteeing their absence.
On non-mainnet networks, the absence of empty accounts is guaranteed only if genesis had no empty accounts AND Spurious Dragon was active from genesis.
After the merge transition completes, any operation that would create an empty account results in undefined behavior; the Spurious Dragon mechanism must prevent this.
After empty account clearing completes pre-merge, the resulting state must contain zero accounts where code is empty AND nonce is zero AND balance is zero.
